reporting-org.narrative:
Iftiin Foundation is a local non-governmental organisation based in Somalia. Ifiin Foundation is empowering young people to become peace makers and drivers of economic growth. The organisation is focused on building a class of independent, self-supporting and community-focused young men and women to serve as agents of social change for a peaceful and stable future.
Iftiin Foundation, Puntland Development and Research Centre (PDRC), YEEL, and City University of Mogadishu have formed The Shaqo Consortium (Jobs Consortium) implementing a ground-breaking three-year initiative. This will be building upon the successes of the 2020-2022 Nexus Skills and Jobs pilot projects, the Shaqo Consortium has embarked on its second phase with the generous support of the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands. At the heart of the Shaqo Consortium’s mission is the imperative to create realistic, sustainable livelihood opportunities for the multitude of unemployed Somali youth aged 15 to 25. Recognizing that the empowerment of this demographic is crucial to the social and economic development of the country, the consortium is dedicated to cultivating a future where young people can thrive and contribute to the fabric of their communities. With the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands as a key partner and advocate, the Shaqo Consortium is poised to make a transformative impact on the lives of Somali youth, unlocking a brighter future for individuals and the nation as a whole.

description.narrative:
Shaqo Platform is a ground-breaking initiative collaboratively implemented by the Iftiin Foundation, Puntland Development and Research Center (PDRC), YEEL, and City University of Mogadishu. Building upon the successes of the Nexus Skills and Jobs Programme pilot projects (2022-2022). The Shaqo Platform has embarked on the second phase of the Nexus Skills and Jobs Programme with the generous support of the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands.
At the heart of Shaqo Platform’s mission is the imperative to create realistic, sustainable livelihood opportunities for the multitude of unemployed Somali youth aged 15 to 25. Recognizing that the empowerment of this demographic is crucial to social and economic development, the Consortium is dedicated to cultivating a future where young people can thrive and contribute to the fabric of their communities. The Shaqo Platform represents a groundbreaking shift from conventional consortium approaches in Somalia.Itisalocally-ledinitiativethatbuildscoalitions across public sector entities, civil society, and the private sector, positioning itself at the forefront of tackling the youth unemployment crisis in Somalia. This approach is distinctive because it not only connects various stakeholders but also actively engages them in creating and implementing solutions for employment challenges faced by Somali youth. With the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Kingdom of the Netherlands as a key partner and advocate, the Shaqo Platform is poised to make a transformative impact on the lives of Somali youth, unlocking a brighter future for individuals and the nation as a whole.
